ei.title: How Fashion Items Got Their Names

fullPassage:
How Fashion Items Got Their Names

Do you know what a jumpsuit is? It is usually a single item that covers your whole body, even your arms and legs. It is easy and quick to put on and to take off. As the name indicates, the jumpsuit began as clothing for jumping from planes. Later, designers transformed this functional design into luxurious women's fashion items seen in fashion shows around the world. Like the jumpsuit, there are other fashion items with interesting stories about how they got their names.

Sneak Up in Sneakers

You have probably owned a pair of sneakers for everyday activities or sports. They are a type of athletic shoe designed specifically to be worn for physical activities and sports. So, why are they called sneakers? The name "sneakers" is derived from the term "to sneak up."

Due to the fact that sneakers' soles are mostly made of rubber, they make little noise when people walk. This allows people who are wearing them to sneak up on others. Before rubber, leather was used for the sole of shoes. Traditional leather shoes make a lot of noise, and it is easier to hear the person wearing them. However, with sneakers, you can quietly sneak up on your friends and surprise them.

Blue Jeans from Genoa

Whether they are loose fit or slim fit, most of you have at least one pair of blue jeans. They were named "jeans" because they were made of jean, a sort of tough cotton cloth. The word jean is a modification of Gênes, the French name of the Italian city of Genoa. In the 17th and 18th centuries, Genoa was a major center for trade. Sailing merchants from Genoa traded their goods throughout Europe, particularly in England and France. One of the items that made Genoa famous was a strong cotton cloth, ideally suited to making tough work clothes. The cloth was most likely colored blue. French was widely spoken in Europe at that time, so the cloth was called "bleu de Gênes" (the blue of Genoa). This is how the pants made with "bleu de Gênes" became known as blue jeans in English.

A Man in a Tuxedo in Tuxedo Park

People wear tuxedos when a formal dress code is required, like for the opera, dinner parties, or awards shows. The tuxedo likely got its name from Tuxedo Park, one of the first gated communities in New York. In the late 19th century, men usually wore jackets with long tails that reached their knees on formal occasions. One evening, a man showed up with a short black jacket without tails in Tuxedo Park. The male guests who stayed there were fascinated by the new jacket and started to wear the same style. Later, more people asked their tailors to make them a jacket "like the one worn in Tuxedo Park." At first, this style of jacket was considered less formal than one with long tails. As more and more men wore the shorter style, it eventually replaced the longer version. Now men's formal wear is the tuxedo. Isn't it ironic that the tuxedo was not originally considered very formal, but now it is the most formal clothing men wear?

Flip-flops, Flip-flop

On beaches and at pools, everyone seems to wear simple shoes with a band across the top of the foot and between the big toe and second toe. Amazingly, they are one of the oldest shoes in history. Ancient Egyptian paintings show they were worn around 4,000 B.C. Due to the fact that they have such a long history, they have different names all around the world. The Japanese call them zories. New Zealanders call them jandals, which is a shortened form of "Japanese sandals." However, in the USA, these shoes are called "flip-flops." Just walk around in a pair of them, and you can easily guess why they got this name. The rubber soles hit the bottom of your feet as you walk, making a flip-flop, flip-flop sound. The sound became the name of the shoes, flip-flops.

Whatever origins these fashion items have, they are being worn by more and more people in various places around the world. Why don't you look for other fashion items that have as interesting name origins as those introduced here?

This allows people who are wearing them to sneak up on others. Before rubber, leather was used for the sole of shoes. Traditional leather shoes make a lot of noise, and it is easier to hear the person wearing them. However, with sneakers, you can quietly sneak up on your friends and surprise them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용으로 알 수 있는 것은?
ch: 전통 가죽 신발은 소리를 거의 내지 않는다.
운동화는 오직 운동 경기에서만 착용할 수 있다.

det.korean: 'sneakers'라는 이름은 'to sneak up(몰래 다가가다)'에서 유래했다(derived).
det.analysis: ✅ ③: 'The name sneakers is derived from the term to sneak up' — 원문 그대로. ❌ ①: rubber(고무)로 만들어짐. ❌ ②: 전통 가죽 신발은 소리가 많이 남. ❌ ④: everyday activities or sports — 일상+운동 모두.
det.tip: 각 선택지를 원문과 대조. ①②는 사실 반대, ④는 범위를 좁혀 왜곡.

questions.passage: They were named "jeans" because they were made of jean, a sort of tough cotton cloth. The word jean is a modification of Gênes, the French name of the Italian city of Genoa. In the 17th and 18th centuries, Genoa was a major center for trade. Sailing merchants from Genoa traded their goods throughout Europe, particularly in England and France. One of the items that made Genoa famous was a strong cotton cloth, ideally suited to making tough work clothes. The cloth was most likely colored blue. French was widely spoken in Europe at that time, so the cloth was called "bleu de Gênes" (the blue of Genoa). This is how the pants made with "bleu de Gênes" became known as blue jeans in English.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: jean이라는 단어는 프랑스어 Gênes에서 변형된 것이다.
제노바 상인들은 특히 영국과 프랑스에서 상품을 거래했다.

det.korean: 면직물은 파란색(blue)이었을 가능성이 높다. 빨간색이 아님.
det.analysis: ❌ ④: 원문은 'most likely colored blue'. 빨간색이 아니라 파란색. ✅ ①②③: 모두 원문과 일치.
det.tip: 'most likely colored blue' — 파란색이었을 가능성이 높다. 이것이 'blue jeans'의 유래.

questions.passage: People wear tuxedos when a formal dress code is required, like for the opera, dinner parties, or awards shows. The tuxedo likely got its name from Tuxedo Park, one of the first gated communities in New York. In the late 19th century, men usually wore jackets with long tails that reached their knees on formal occasions. One evening, a man showed up with a short black jacket without tails in Tuxedo Park. The male guests who stayed there were fascinated by the new jacket and started to wear the same style. At first, this style of jacket was considered less formal than one with long tails. As more and more men wore the shorter style, it eventually replaced the longer version.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 턱시도파크에서 한 남자가 긴 꼬리가 달린 재킷을 입고 나타났다.
19세기 후반 남성들은 짧은 재킷을 정장으로 입었다.
턱시도는 처음부터 가장 격식 있는 옷으로 여겨졌다.
턱시도파크에서 한 남자가 꼬리가 없는 짧은 검은 재킷을 입고 나타났다.

det.korean: 턱시도파크에서 꼬리 없는 짧은 검은 재킷을 입은 남자가 나타났다
det.analysis:
✅ ② 꼬리 없는 짧은 검은 재킷 — 원문: 'a short black jacket without tails in Tuxedo Park'
❌ ① 긴 꼬리 재킷 — 원문: without tails(꼬리 없음)
❌ ③ 짧은 재킷이 정장 — 원문: 'men usually wore jackets with long tails'(긴 꼬리가 정장)
❌ ④ 처음부터 격식 — 원문: 'not originally considered very formal'
det.tip: without tails = 꼬리 없는. showed up = 나타났다.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 빈칸에 알맞은 영어 단어를 쓰시오.

이 면직물은 튼튼한 작업복을 만드는 데 이상적으로 __________했다.
(적합한: s__________)

det.korean: 적합한 = suited. ideally suited to ~에 이상적으로 적합한.
det.analysis:
정답: suited
허용 답안: suited, Suited
det.tip: suited to: ~에 적합한. suit(적합하다)의 과거분사/형용사.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 빈칸에 알맞은 영어 단어를 쓰시오.

짧은 스타일이 결국 긴 버전을 __________했다.
(대체하다: r__________)

det.korean: 대체하다 = replaced. eventually replaced the longer version.
det.analysis:
정답: replaced
허용 답안: replaced, Replaced
det.tip: replace: 대체하다. re(다시) + place(놓다) = 다시 놓다 → 대체하다.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 빈칸에 알맞은 영어 단어를 쓰시오.

턱시도가 원래 매우 격식 있는 것으로 여겨지지 않았지만 지금은 가장 격식 있는 옷이라니 __________하지 않은가?
(역설적인: i__________)

det.korean: 역설적인 = ironic. 기대와 현실의 반전을 나타내는 형용사.
det.analysis:
정답: ironic
허용 답안: ironic, Ironic
det.tip: ironic: 예상과 다른 결과가 나올 때 사용. irony(아이러니)의 형용사형.

questions.passage: On beaches and at pools, everyone seems to wear simple shoes with a band across the top of the foot and between the big toe and second toe. Amazingly, they are one of the oldest shoes in history. Ancient Egyptian paintings show they were worn around 4,000 B.C. Due to the fact that they have such a long history, they have different names all around the world. The Japanese call them zories. New Zealanders call them jandals, which is a shortened form of "Japanese sandals." However, in the USA, these shoes are called "flip-flops." Just walk around in a pair of them, and you can easily guess why they got this name. The rubber soles hit the bottom of your feet as you walk, making a flip-flop, flip-flop sound.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 플립플롭이라는 이름은 걸을 때 나는 소리에서 유래했다.

det.korean: 플립플롭이라는 이름은 걸을 때 나는 소리에서 유래했다
det.analysis:
✅ ② 걸을 때 나는 소리에서 유래 — 원문: 'making a flip-flop sound. The sound became the name'
❌ ① 20세기에 처음 — 원문: 'around 4,000 B.C.'(역사상 가장 오래된 신발 중 하나)
❌ ③ 뉴질랜드=조리 — 원문: 일본이 zories, 뉴질랜드는 jandals
❌ ④ 가죽 밑창 — 원문: 'rubber soles'(고무 밑창)
det.tip: flip-flop sound → flip-flops. 의성어에서 유래한 이름.

questions.passage: Do you know what a jumpsuit is? It is usually a single item that covers your whole body, even your arms and legs. It is easy and quick to put on and to take off. As the name indicates, the jumpsuit began as clothing for jumping from planes. Later, designers transformed this functional design into luxurious women's fashion items seen in fashion shows around the world. Like the jumpsuit, there are other fashion items with interesting stories about how they got their names.
questions.stem: 점프수트에 대한 다음 글의 내용으로 알 수 있는 것은?

det.korean: 점프수트는 원래 비행기에서 뛰어내리는 의복으로 시작했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②: 'began as clothing for jumping from planes' — 원문 그대로. ❌ ①: 팔과 다리를 덮는다(covers). ❌ ③: 디자이너가 발명한 것이 아니라 변형(transformed)한 것. ❌ ④: 여성(women's) 패션 아이템.
det.tip: covers(덮다) ≠ 노출. transformed(변형) ≠ invented(발명). women's ≠ men's.

questions.passage: Whatever origins these fashion items have, they are being worn by more and more people in various places around the world. Why don't you look for other fashion items that have as interesting name origins as those introduced here? Do you know what a jumpsuit is? As the name indicates, the jumpsuit began as clothing for jumping from planes. The name "sneakers" is derived from the term "to sneak up." The word jean is a modification of Gênes. The tuxedo likely got its name from Tuxedo Park. The rubber soles hit the bottom of your feet as you walk, making a flip-flop, flip-flop sound.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 소개된 패션 아이템의 이름 유래를 잘못 설명한 것은?
ch: jeans — 이탈리아 도시 제노바의 프랑스어 이름에서 유래

det.korean: 플립플롭은 모양이 아니라 걸을 때 나는 소리에서 이름이 유래했다.
det.analysis: ❌ ④: 원문은 'making a flip-flop, flip-flop sound. The sound became the name' — 소리에서 유래. ✅ ①②③: 모두 원문과 일치하는 설명.
det.tip: flip-flops의 이름 유래 = 소리(sound). 모양(shape)이 아님.
